claim.pdf_says: Printed page 545 (PDF page 575) ends with '4) All instance objects are destroyed.' followed only by the footer. The block that begins 'NOTE  Any open files in an object are closed before the object is destroyed.' and runs through '14.6.13.1.1  General / An exception condition is either a condition associated with a specific exception status indicator or an exception object. ... specified in the RAISING phrase.' is printed EXACTLY ONCE, on printed page 546 (PDF page 576).
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md carries that entire page-576 body TWICE. First inside the page-575 slice at lines 24070-24108 (a stray '---', then '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', 'NOTE Any open files in an object are closed before the object is destroyed.', items 5)-7), '## 14.6.12 Abnormal run unit termination', ... '## 14.6.13.1.1 General', '... specified in the RAISING phrase.'), and again at lines 24110-24147 under ' / ## Page 576'.
claim.why_it_matters: About 40 lines of normative text for 14.6.11 items 5)-7), 14.6.12 and 14.6.13/14.6.13.1/14.6.13.1.1 are duplicated verbatim. The duplicate also re-emits the anchors '<a id="section-14-6-12">', '<a id="section-14-6-13">', '<a id="section-14-6-13-1">' and '<a id="section-14-6-13-1-1">', so every intra-document link to those sections resolves to the copy that has no page anchor and the wrong heading depths. Any grep-based citation workflow gets two hits for one rule and cannot tell which is canonical.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides, and the attempts to refute all failed. PDF SIDE (rendered at 300 dpi, read directly). - PDF page 575 = printed page 545 (footer reads '(c)ISO/IEC 2023 545'). Its body runs 14.6.9.4 Space filling a dynamic table -> 14.6.10 Overlapping operands (items 1)-2), NOTE 1, the 'Similarly, ...' paragraph, NOTE 2, the reference-modification paragraph) -> 14.6.11 Normal run unit termination, items 1) through 4). The last line of body text on the page is '4) All instance objects are destroyed.' Below it there is nothing but white space, the '(c)ISO/IEC 2023 545' footer and the licensee line. There is NO NOTE, no items 5)-7), no 14.6.12, no 14.6.13 on this page. So the page-575 slice legitimately ends at item 4). - PDF page 576 = printed page 546 (footer reads '546 (c)ISO/IEC 2023'). Its body is exactly the disputed block, in this order: the indented 'NOTE Any open files in an object are closed before the object is destroyed.', items 5), 6), 7), heading '14.6.12 Abnormal run unit termination' with its five paragraphs and NOTE, heading '14.6.13 Exception condition handling', '14.6.13.1 Exception conditions', '14.6.13.1.1 General', and the closing paragraph 'An exception condition is either a condition associated with a specific exception status indicator or an exception object. ... in which the object is specified in the RAISING phrase.' It is printed ONCE, on this page only. MARKDOWN SIDE (exact line numbers verified by grep, not by the workunit slice alone). - Line 24032 ''. Item '4) All instance objects are destroyed.' is at 24070. Then, still inside the page-575 slice, line 24073 is a stray horizontal rule '---', 24075 is a stray H1 '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', and 24077 begins 'NOTE Any open files in an object are closed before the object is destroyed.' The interpolated block runs to 24109, the '...specified in the RAISING phrase.' paragraph. - Line 24113 '' / '## Page 576' / '**ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)**', then 24118 repeats 'NOTE Any open files in an object are closed before the object is destroyed.' and the same block runs to 24150. - diff of 24077-24109 against 24118-24150 returns only two differing lines, both heading depth: '## 14.6.13.1 Exception conditions' vs '### 14.6.13.1 Exception conditions', and '## 14.6.13.1.1 General' vs '#### 14.6.13.1.1 General'. Every other line, including all normative prose, is byte-identical. This is a verbatim duplication, not a reflow, not a page-break artifact, not two different renderings of adjacent material. - Duplicate anchors confirmed by grep: section-14-6-12 at 24085 and 24126; section-14-6-13 at 24100 and 24141; section-14-6-13-1 at 24103 and 24144; section-14-6-13-1-1 at 24106 and 24147. Four id collisions, so an HTML/anchor consumer resolves each link to the FIRST occurrence, which is the spurious copy stranded inside the page-575 slice. REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED. - 'The text is merely reflowed / on an adjacent line': no. Both copies are present in full, 33 lines each, verbatim identical. - 'Only page-break furniture': no. The stray '---' and stray H1 ARE furniture, but they are the LEADER of ~35 lines of duplicated NORMATIVE text (items 5)-7) of 14.6.11, all of 14.6.12, and the opening of 14.6.13). - 'Formatting only, meaning unchanged': the prose meaning of each copy is the same, but the DOCUMENT is changed: 14.6.11 items 5)-7), 14.6.12 and 14.6.13.1.1 each exist twice, and clause 14.6.12's rules appear to be stated twice in one standard. A conformance citation workflow cannot tell which hit is canonical. - 'The claim misquotes a source': the quoted text is accurate on both sides. Only the line-number ranges are slightly off (see below). Minor inaccuracies in the claim, none of which affect the verdict: the stray block is at 24073-24109 (not 24070-24108) and the page-576 copy at 24113-24150 (not 24110-24147); line 24070 is item '4)' itself, which is correct page-575 content. The claim's characterization of the consequence is right: the surviving-first copy is the one with no page anchor and with the flattened '##' heading depths, so anchors and heading-derived TOCs both land on the interloper.
verdict.corrected_description: specs/ISO_COBOL.md duplicates the entire printed-page-546 body. PDF page 576 (printed 546) carries it exactly once: the NOTE 'Any open files in an object are closed before the object is destroyed.', 14.6.11 items 5) 6) 7), all of 14.6.12 Abnormal run unit termination, and 14.6.13 / 14.6.13.1 / 14.6.13.1.1 General through '...specified in the RAISING phrase.' PDF page 575 (printed 545) ends cleanly at '4) All instance objects are destroyed.' with nothing after it but the footer. In the markdown, that block appears twice: a spurious copy stranded inside the page-575 slice at lines 24073-24109, introduced by a stray '---' rule (24073) and a stray H1 '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' (24075); and the correct copy in the page-576 slice at 24113-24150. A diff of the two ranges shows they are byte-identical except for two heading-depth lines: the stray copy flattens '### 14.6.13.1 Exception conditions' to '##' and '#### 14.6.13.1.1 General' to '##'. Four section anchors are emitted twice (section-14-6-12 at 24085/24126, section-14-6-13 at 24100/24141, section-14-6-13-1 at 24103/24144, section-14-6-13-1-1 at 24106/24147); since the spurious copy comes first in file order, every intra-document link and every heading-derived TOC entry resolves to the copy that sits under the wrong page anchor and at the wrong heading depth, and the stray H1 additionally breaks the heading hierarchy mid-clause-14. Fix: delete lines 24073-24110 (the stray rule, the stray H1, and the duplicated block plus its trailing blank), leaving the page-575 slice to end at '4) All instance objects are destroyed.'
